accuracy.evidence: Layer sizes and temperatures checked against USGS 'The Earth's Interior' and BGS 'Inside the Earth': mean radius 6,371 km; oceanic crust 5–10 km and continental crust 30–70 km (35 km used as a typical continental figure); mantle about 2,890–2,900 km; outer core about 2,200 km thick; inner core radius about 1,220 km; temperatures rise with depth (Moho ~500–1,000 °C, core–mantle boundary ~3,700 °C, centre ~5,000–5,400 °C, comparable to the photosphere). The mantle is described as mostly solid rock that creeps, not a sea of lava; the inner core is solid because of pressure (PREM; Jeanloz). The thickness step labels the inner core '1,220 km to the centre' so radius is not confused with a shell thickness.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets well-documented Earth-science ideas (AAAS Project 2061; King 2010, research on children's ideas about the Earth's interior; Lillo 1994): Earth is hollow or full of water or fire (step 1 predict 'An empty space' / 'Water all the way down'), the mantle is a sea of lava (Ali, p5, tag lava), the crust is the thickest layer because diagrams draw it thick (Dev, p3, tag thick), the core is cold or icy (Gus, Hana), and the hottest inner core must be liquid (Leo, m8, tag squeeze). The solid/liquid sort and the 'crust drawn thicker' note on the cut-away confront the last two directly.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). 932 Earth Is Made of Rock (flagrock) is about bedrock under soil, 560 What Is a Volcano (flagvolc) is about magma reaching the surface, and 617 Fast & Slow Earth Changes looks at weathering and eruptions; none drills a four-layer cut-away, compares true thicknesses on a bar (so the crust shrinks to a line), or has the learner sort the mantle as solid and the outer core as liquid.

lab_teaches.evidence: The drill makes the four layers appear in order as depth increases, so 'under the crust is hot rock, then metal' is found, not told. Naming is done on the cut-away itself. The thickness bars use true kilometres, so the crust becomes a sliver and the 'apple-skin' comparison is seen. The heat order and the solid/liquid sort separate 'hot' from 'liquid', which is the key idea for the mantle and the inner core.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options the later task disproves: 'An empty space' under the crust, 'The crust' at the very centre, 'The mantle' as the thinnest layer, and 'At the crust' as the hottest place. The done message reports the learner's prediction against the answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with tagged wrong answers: deep (we live on the crust), thick (the crust is thinnest: 35 km against the mantle's 2,900 km), hot (hotter towards the centre), lava (the mantle is mostly solid rock that creeps), cold, squeeze (pressure keeps the inner core solid), and order (outside in: crust, mantle, outer core, inner core). Lab mistakes are named too, e.g. 'The crust is thinner than the mantle. Look at the bars: 35 km.' and 'The inner core is squeezed so hard that it stays solid metal.'

readability.evidence: validate_lessons readability passed (kid under 6.5, adult under 9.5). Kid sentences are short and use the precise terms crust, mantle, outer core, inner core, solid, liquid and metal. Canvas text is one short instruction per step, and buttons say exactly what they do (Drill deeper, Put on: Centre, Crust, Solid, Bea is right).

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases and explanation similarity under 12% to all lessons. Each kid paragraph carries one idea (crust we live on; thick hot solid mantle; metal core, liquid then solid; crust thinnest, hotter with depth). The adult text gives sizes from named sources, the task order and the named slips.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light theme for every step before, during and after Show me (/workspace/shots/lay-*). After the first pass the Crust label was moved just outside the rim so it no longer sat in the mantle, and the 'drawn thicker' note was moved under the cut-away so it does not cover the drill. Thickness bars, Solid/Liquid tiles and statement cards span the width; tap targets are over 44 px tall.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all six tasks complete with Show me, challenge shown, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors. Every drag or tap has a button (Drill deeper, Put on: Outside layer, Crust, Solid, Eli is right), and the canvas aria-label states the drill depth, layers reached, names placed and the order so far after each action.
